pass_b_english: We are burdened with the weight of sin from our ancient transgressions.
The prophet declares that the Lord was pleased with his land and forgave the iniquities of his people, covering all their sins.
This beatitude applies to both the circumcised and the Gentiles, as Paul explains in his letter to the Romans.
We are justified in Christ, who was handed over for our transgressions and raised for our justification.
If Christ was not raised, then those who have fallen asleep in Christ have perished.
But the prophet assures us that the dead will rise, and those in the tombs will be raised, each receiving the reward they deserve.
God is the judge of all, and now Christ has been raised from the dead, the firstfruits of those who have fallen asleep.
The first man, Adam, fell into sin and became the beginning of those who slipped into corruption, and death came into the world through him.
Just as Adam was the first to fall, so too will all people be justified through the resurrection of the dead, which comes through a man, Jesus Christ.
The mystery of the divine economy is revealed in the fact that it was necessary for a man to conquer death on our behalf, and this is precisely what the Word of God, who became man, accomplished.
He did not take the form of angels but of the seed of Abraham, so that he might be like his brothers in all things.
In this way, he was able to heal the fallen and to overcome death through obedience and righteousness, which is the opposite of the transgression and sin that led to death.
The Son of God, who did not know sin, became man, so that just as all were condemned in Adam, so all might be justified in Christ and put off the death that came from sin.
As the apostle Paul says, 'just as through the disobedience of the one man the many were made sinners, so also through the obedience of the one man the many will be made righteous.' (Romans 5:19)
Through our transgressions, Christ was given over to death, but for our justification, he was raised to life.
As a result, we who are in him have also been raised to new life.
The Word of God, which is life itself, has been bestowed not just on Christ's physical body, but on the entirety of human nature.
Christ, as the firstfruits of those who have fallen asleep, has been raised from the dead, and in due time, the rest of humanity will also be brought to life.
However, this resurrection will not occur in a chaotic or disorderly manner, but rather in a way that is both organized and discerning, with each person being raised in their proper time.
